intended_object: The defining Hopf ideal I ⊆ H of the stabilizer of a subspace W ⊆ M in an affine group scheme G = Spec H over a field k acting on the comodule M. This is the closed subgroup G_W whose A-points g satisfy g(A⊗W) = A⊗W (Milne, Algebraic Groups, Ch. 4; Humphreys §13). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The ideal is the span of two sets of elements. The first is the matrix coefficients c(ψ∘q, w) = (ψ∘q ⊗ id)(ρ(w)), for w ∈ W and ψ a functional on M/W. The second is the antipodes of those coefficients. A point g : H → A kills the first set exactly when the coaction sends A⊗W into A⊗W. Over a field, this works because functionals on M/W separate its points. A point g kills the antipodes exactly when g⁻¹ also sends A⊗W into A⊗W. Together, the two conditions say that g carries A⊗W onto itself, which is the stabilizer. This also covers infinite-dimensional M, where the condition g(W) ⊆ W alone does not define a subgroup. The proof obligations show that the span is a Hopf ideal: comultiplication, counit and antipode are all compatible with it. So the quotient H/I is the coordinate ring of the closed subgroup G_W.

The library's characterization theorems match the textbook object. Its A-points are those preserving A⊗W. It is the smallest Hopf ideal containing the coefficients. It is ⊥ exactly when W is a subcomodule. Its Lie algebra is the stabilizer of W under the differentiated representation.

Working over a field is the natural setting: the construction relies on duals of M/W separating points. It also matches the textbook setting of affine algebraic groups. Mathlib has no stabilizer Hopf ideal or comparable notion.
